Sudha: which one, thermo?
Mohit: yeah. I've drawn the whole classroom in my notebook
Sudha: I saw you yawning. Did you sleep at all last night?
Mohit: 3 hours maybe. Project deadlines
Sudha: so is it boredom or tiredness
Mohit: honestly both. I can't tell
Sudha: the hard bit is when they overlap. Try a walk at the break and some water, not more coffee
Mohit: fine 🙂 also I'm going to sleep properly tonight
Sudha: good. I'll share my notes on the last part if you're lost

subtype: Bored and tired in study life [Expressing]
passage: The village college in Chinmay's town ran lectures through a loudspeaker in a hall with a tin roof, and by two o'clock the heat pressed down on everyone. Chinmay had been up since five to help his father at the mill. He was doodling a bullock cart in the margin. His eyes closed for a second; he jerked them open. Beside him, Eshaan was on his phone under the desk. The lecturer's voice droned on about tax law. At the break Chinmay splashed his face at the tap and sat under the neem tree. Eshaan joined him. "Bored?" "Tired," Chinmay said, "and also bored." They agreed to swap notes and try to sleep early.

qa.q: What did Chinmay doodle in the margin?
qa.a: He doodled a bullock cart.

qa.q: What might Chinmay be feeling in the hall, and what might be adding to it?
qa.a: He may feel both bored and worn out, since he had been up since five helping his father at the mill and the heat and drone added to it.

qa.q: What small step could help Chinmay through afternoons like this?
qa.a: Splashing his face, taking a break in the shade, swapping notes with Eshaan and getting to bed early could help.

qa.q: How might Eshaan's phone use look to the lecturer?
qa.a: The lecturer might read it as not caring, though Eshaan could be tired or bored like Chinmay.

grounding: Chinmay shows yawns and doodling from boredom overlapping with tiredness in a dull hot lecture.

subtype: Bored and tired in study life [Expressing]
passage: In a lecture hall in Prague, Vera sat through the third hour of Statistics II. The professor's voice was flat, the slides dense. Vera's eyes drooped. She yawned twice, then began doodling spirals in the margin of her notes. Beside her, Clara was scrolling her phone under the desk. At the break Clara said, "God, so boring." Vera rubbed her eyes. "I'm not even sure I'm bored. I slept four hours. I worked the café closing shift." Clara looked at her more closely. "You've done that every night this week." "Rent," Vera shrugged. They sat quietly. Then Clara said, "Let's split the lecture notes. You take the first half, I'll do the second. And maybe ask the café to move one shift?" Vera nodded slowly. The next week she swapped one closing shift for a Saturday morning, and stayed awake through the whole of Statistics II.

qa.q: How many hours had Vera slept?
qa.a: Four hours.

qa.q: What was Vera feeling during the lecture?
qa.a: She was exhausted more than bored, yawning and doodling after closing shifts every night.

qa.q: Which small changes helped Vera stay awake the next week?
qa.a: Splitting notes with Clara and swapping one late shift for a Saturday morning to get more rest.

qa.q: How did Clara first read the lecture and Vera's yawns?
qa.a: Clara saw it as plain boredom, until Vera explained the late shifts and lack of sleep.

grounding: Shows a young adult whose yawns and doodling mix boredom and tiredness, and how structure and rest help.

subtype: Bored and tired in study life [Expressing]
passage: It was week ten of the most overloaded semester Shalini had ever had: six courses, two projects and a part-time tutoring job. In the college library, she sat with a textbook open and read the same paragraph four times. Then she picked up her phone and scrolled for twenty minutes without noticing. Her friend Bhavna, at the next desk, watched her yawn, doodle a cat, check her phone again. "You okay? You seem bored out of your mind." Shalini laughed weakly. "I'm not bored. I'm fried. I can't tell the difference anymore." Bhavna took her phone and put it in her own bag. "Try this. Twenty-five minutes of reading, then five minutes walking. I'll give the phone back at the break." Shalini tried it. By the third round she had actually finished a chapter. That night, for the first time in weeks, she slept at eleven.

qa.q: How many courses was Shalini taking?
qa.a: Six courses.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling in the library?
qa.a: She was exhausted and fried, unable to tell boredom from tiredness, reading the same paragraph four times.

qa.q: What small structure helped Shalini focus?
qa.a: Bhavna's plan of twenty-five minutes of reading and a five-minute walk, with the phone kept away until the break.

qa.q: How did Bhavna first read Shalini's yawns and doodling?
qa.a: Bhavna thought Shalini seemed bored, until Shalini explained she was fried from overload.

grounding: Shows a young adult in an overloaded semester showing boredom and tiredness through yawns, doodling and phone use, and how structure helps.

subtype: Bored and tired in study life [Expressing]
passage:
Dear Hemant bhaiya,
You asked how the new semester is going, and I didn't want to just say "fine" again.
Honestly, I'm bored in some classes and exhausted in all of them. In the economics lecture I doodle the whole time. In the evening I scroll for an hour and then feel guilty. I thought I'd become lazy.
Then last week the college nurse asked how much I sleep. Five hours, most nights. She said that alone could make every lecture feel dull.
So I'm trying a few things. Phone out of the room at night. Bed by eleven. A short walk after lunch. In the dull lecture, I've started writing one question for the teacher every fifteen minutes, just to stay with it.
It's only been four days, but I yawn less. Will tell you more on Sunday's call.
Love,
Shalini

qa.q: How much does Shalini sleep most nights?
qa.a: Five hours.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling before the nurse's question?
qa.a: Shalini felt bored and exhausted, and guilty, worrying about becoming lazy.

qa.q: What changes is Shalini trying, and why might they help?
qa.a: Phone out of the room, bed by eleven, a walk after lunch and writing questions in lectures, which add rest and structure.

qa.q: How did the college nurse see Shalini's dull lectures?
qa.a: The nurse thought lack of sleep alone could make every lecture feel dull.

grounding: Shows a young adult noticing that boredom and tiredness overlap and using rest and structure to feel more engaged.

subtype: Bored and tired in study life [Expressing]
passage: You asked why I'm suddenly awake in Thermodynamics, Madhuri. Honestly? I'm Pradeep, and last semester I was a mess. In every lecture I'd yawn so wide my jaw clicked, fill the margins with doodled robots, and scroll my phone under the desk. Professor Nair once stopped mid-sentence and asked if the class was keeping me up. I blamed the lectures; they were dull, sure. But the truth was I was sleeping at three every night, gaming or watching videos, then running to an eight o'clock class. Bored and exhausted looked exactly the same on me, and I couldn't tell which was which. So I tried an experiment for three weeks: phone in the drawer at midnight, a ten-minute walk between the two morning lectures, and notes in a grid so my hands had something to do besides robots. The lectures didn't get more exciting. But I stopped yawning, and I understood entropy for the first time. Mostly, it was sleep.

qa.q: What did Pradeep doodle in the margins?
qa.a: Robots.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling in those lectures?
qa.a: Pradeep felt bored and exhausted at once, the two blurring together because of sleeping at three every night.

qa.q: What did Pradeep's three-week experiment include?
qa.a: Phone in the drawer at midnight, a ten-minute walk between the morning lectures, and grid notes to keep the hands busy.

qa.q: How might Professor Nair have read Pradeep's yawns?
qa.a: As a sign that the lecture was boring Pradeep, which is why the professor asked, half-joking, if the class was keeping Pradeep up.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult showing yawns, doodling and phone use in lectures, where boredom and tiredness overlap, and structure, breaks and rest help.
